Meet BrewGo from Fernhollow Coffee Roasters
Ordering your morning coffee just got easier. Fernhollow Coffee Roasters has launched BrewGo, our brand-new mobile app that lets you place and pay for your order right from your phone, before you ever set foot in the shop.
No more waiting in line. Tap your order, choose a pickup time, and your drink will be freshly made and waiting for you the moment you walk through the door. Spend your break enjoying your coffee, not standing in line.
BrewGo also remembers what you love. The app saves every order you have placed before, so your usual latte or weekend treat is just one tap away. Reordering your favorite takes seconds, with no need to search the menu again.
To celebrate the launch, we are giving every new user 20 percent off their very first order placed through the app. Download BrewGo today, create your free account, and claim the discount at checkout.
BrewGo works at all 18 Fernhollow Coffee Roasters cafes. Search for BrewGo in your app store and start ordering the smarter way.

Rowan Hill Homeware · 118 Aldergate Street · Millpond 4021
3 June
Dear HomeGuard Protection Plan Member,
Thank you for being a valued member of our HomeGuard Protection Plan. Because your membership entitles you to complimentary care events throughout the year, we are delighted to invite you to a free hands-on maintenance workshop held at our store. The session is offered at no charge, and this invitation is being sent to our plan members only.
During the workshop you will learn how to clean, adjust, and prolong the life of the kitchen appliances and cookware we carry, and you will also preview several new items arriving this season. The session will be led by Coledale Appliance Specialists, a repair and servicing firm whose technicians are certified to open and recalibrate the motors and heating elements that our own staff are not trained to handle. Their guidance will help you keep the products you already own running safely for years. Although Rowan Hill Homeware has served the Millpond area for 22 years, this is the first time we have brought in outside experts of this kind.
Seating is limited, so early booking is encouraged. Two identical sessions will be held on Saturday, 14 June, at our Aldergate Street shop, one beginning at 10 a.m. and one at 2 p.m. To reserve a place in either session, please telephone our Events Desk at 03 5567 2200. Our website lists our full product range but is not used for workshop bookings.
We hope to see you there.
Warm regards,
Rowan Hill Homeware

part7.title: Bài đọc 8 (Câu 164 - 167)
part7.passageText:
Made to Last: The Quiet Craft of Fairholme
By Adrian Colville
For more than thirty years, Fairholme has built a quiet reputation among people who care how a machine is made. Every model leaving its small workshop begins with a hand-brazed steel frame, a broad spread of gears for climbing and descending, and hand-laced wheels chosen for strength rather than weight.
Its founders remain sure that a frame built slowly will outlast several cheaper ones. Each joint is filed and polished before painting, and every finished frame is tested to be certain it can
handle
years of daily use on rough ground.
Fairholme makes no effort to court racers or weekend competitors. Its owners are the people who ride the same route to work each morning, carry shopping home each evening, and expect a machine ready to go in any weather.
One detail that longtime owners praise is the fully enclosed chain cover. By sealing the chain away from rain and grit, it saves riders from marking their clothes when they set out in ordinary dress rather than cycling gear. A built-in dynamo, meanwhile, powers the lamps, sparing riders the worry of flat batteries after dark.
Whatever the model, the goal stays the same: a machine that asks little and serves for many years.

Pemberton Business Network
42 Calderwood Street
12 September
Dear Ms. Ackroyd,
On behalf of the entire committee, I am pleased to inform you that Ackroyd Ceramics has been chosen as a finalist in this year's Pemberton Enterprise Awards. Being named a finalist is a significant honor, and the winners in each category will be announced during the ceremony itself.
Now in its ninth year, our program continues to celebrate outstanding local businesses. Nominations were submitted by members of the community and then reviewed by an independent selection panel. Nominations for this year closed in August. The finalists represent five categories: retail, hospitality, craft manufacturing, community service, and innovation. A cash prize will be awarded to the winner named in each category. Last year's overall winner, Foxton Leatherworks, will help present this year's awards.
The ceremony will feature a short talk by Bernadette Lowry. Ms. Lowry began her career in Canada before opening her own firm in our region, and she now devotes much of her time to mentoring young business owners. She has also announced that she will step back from her role as director of that firm next year.
The ceremony will be held on 18 October at Redmayne Hall, beginning at 6:30 P.M. A reception with refreshments will follow. Parking is available in the lot beside the hall. As this is an invitation-only event with limited seating, please confirm your attendance by 4 October.
Sincerely,
Malcolm Everhart
Awards Director, Pemberton Business Network
Telephone 555-0148 or e-mail
[email protected]

Welcome to Larkfield Dance Studio
Since opening its doors in Cedar Valley, Larkfield Dance Studio has built its name on youth instruction. Every one of our current weekly classes serves students between the ages of six and seventeen, from first-time movers to competition-ready teens, and generations of local families have passed through our doors.
Meet Your Instructor
Lorena Bassett joined the Larkfield team last year. Before turning to teaching, she danced with several touring companies across South America, and for the past eight years she has coached adult learners at community centers, guiding people who arrive with no experience at all. Warm and patient, she is known for putting nervous newcomers at ease within their first lesson.
Our Space
Larkfield occupies a bright, ground-floor studio on Maple Row. Our two mirrored rooms can each comfortably
accommodate
up to thirty dancers, the floors are sprung for safety, and a small lounge just off the entrance gives waiting families a comfortable place to sit.
Starting Soon
This autumn we are opening a new evening course, Ballroom Basics, created for adults who are stepping onto the dance floor for the very first time. Beginning Monday, October 6, instructor Lorena Bassett will lead the group each Monday evening across an eight-week term. The term fee is $95. Places are limited, so early sign-up is encouraged.
----------------------
https://www.cedarvalleyliving.com/community
Grown-Ups Finally Get Their Turn at Larkfield
By Damon Whitby | Cedar Valley Living | September 22
For years, Larkfield Dance Studio has been a familiar fixture for Cedar Valley's youngest dancers. This October, the Maple Row studio is trying something rather different: a beginners' course built entirely for adults, and one that its organizers hope will draw people who assumed their dancing days had passed them by.
The eight-week program, called First Steps on the Floor, begins Monday, October 6 and will be led by instructor Lorena Bassett. Aimed squarely at people who have never taken a dance class of any kind, the course walks students through the fundamentals of ballroom dancing at an unhurried pace. Organizers are also quick to note that no partner is required to sign up.
"So many adults tell me they have always wanted to try this, but they were afraid of being the only beginner in the room," said Bassett. "This class is for exactly those people. Nobody here is expected to know a single step on day one."
The term costs $95, and registration is available only through the studio's website at www.larkfielddance.com.

To: All Staff
From: Trevor Osei
Date: February 24
Subject: New employee commuter shuttle
Hello everyone,
Beginning Monday, March 3, the Delmara Group will operate a morning commuter shuttle for staff, and I am pleased to say it will be offered at no cost to employees. The service was arranged to ease the pressure on our limited on-site parking and to give everyone a dependable alternative for the morning journey to work.
To reserve a seat, please register for one of the routes shown on the attached schedule no later than February 28. Seats on each route are limited, and they will be assigned in the order that requests are received.

To: Julian Prescott
From: Theresa Boland
Date: September 3
Subject: Venue proposals for the offsite meeting
Hi Julian,
Our annual staff offsite meeting is set for October, and we need to settle on a location soon. Harriet Blaine will be coordinating the site visits and confirming availability once we have narrowed the list down.
Please contact the candidate venues on our shortlist and request a formal proposal from each one, using the comparison you put together for last year's meeting as a guide. Forward each proposal to Harriet as it comes in so that she can begin arranging visits. Once they are all in, combine them into a single comparison sheet for me. I plan to include it in the recommendation I am submitting to the chief operations officer.
Thanks,
Theresa
----------------------
To: Theresa Boland
From: Julian Prescott
Date: September 15
Subject: Re: Venue proposals for the offsite meeting
Attachment: Venue Comparison
Hi Theresa,
The proposals are all in now. According to Harriet Blaine, four of the six venues we contacted returned a completed proposal, which is a stronger response than we had for last year's meeting. The figures are broadly in line with what we saw then, although Harriet did point out one surprise: the daily rate quoted by one of the venues came in well below all of the others.
The full comparison is attached. Let me know if you need anything further before you send it on to Ms. Calloway, or whether she would also like copies of the original proposals.
Julian

To: Northgate Reel Rewards Members
From: Lorna Fitzgerald
Subject: Introducing Northgate Reel Rewards
Date: March 12
Attachment: Rewards Catalog
Dear Member,
Thank you for being part of the Northgate Cinemas community. We are pleased to introduce Northgate Reel Rewards, our new points-based program that lets you earn points on every ticket and concession purchase and exchange those points for a range of rewards.
All members begin at the Matinee level. At this level you earn one point for every dollar you spend, and you may redeem your points for any reward marked for Matinee members in the attached catalog.
Once you have spent three hundred dollars within a single calendar year, you are automatically moved up to the Marquee level. Marquee members earn two points for every dollar spent and may redeem their points for any reward marked for the Marquee level. They also enjoy one benefit reserved for this level alone: invitations to our members-only advance screenings, where you can watch selected films before they open to the general public.
To claim a reward, please review the attached catalog and confirm the points and level required for the item you want. Please note that each reward may be claimed only by members at the level shown beside it. Reply to this message with your choice, and we will verify your balance and arrange delivery or pickup.
Enjoy the show,
Lorna Fitzgerald
Membership Coordinator, Northgate Cinemas

I would very much like to claim the fleece cinema blanket from the catalog. Could you let me know whether my current balance is enough for it, and, if it is not, which reward I would be able to claim instead?

Malcolm Reeves
